items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: And a fine pianist by the name of Eddie Beale. He would play.

ctx.x: Very definitely. In fact this has to be the most serious point of my career, and where I really got the

right kind of guidance from Art Tatum as well as many others, particularly Art Tatum. As I said, in this house, these professionals who were then successful people, came there and played every night. Art Tatum just happened to be the star, and the fact of the matter is Art would sit around and drink a little beer and talk. He was very intellectual, very kind gentleman. And most all of the other pianists would come in and play. King Cole would come in and play and he'd sing. And a fine pianist by the name of Eddie…

I played occasionally although I was a little bit ashamed to follow these men. Occasionally before they came I would have enough nerve to sit down and play, because my friend encouraged me, and they all were very encouraging. But I got to know Art Tatum there briefly at the house, and then I remember one time I was playing in a club where they had these jam sessions and I didn't know the chord changes to the "Sweet Lorraine". As I said at this time I was still studying and really learning, you know, these chord…
